title: Monitoring Phase Transformation in Single Layer 1T’-WS2 Utilizing In-Situ Time-Resolved 4D STEM in SEM
content: The method of 4-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy, performed in Scanning Electron Microscope (4D STEM in SEM) is an emerging analytical/imaging technique inspired by 4D STEM in Transmission Electron Microscope (TEM). Compared with its TEM-based cousin, 4D STEM in SEM offers lower voltage (kV) capability suitable for non-destructive inspection of 2D or beam-sensitive materials. Moreover, various lamellae prepared in SEM equipped with a Focused Ion Beam (FIB) could be directly analyzed by this methodology right after the lift-out procedure. Especially thin, electron-transparent samples could benefit from the described analytical approach.
